card.title: Biomolecules: Introduction and functions of carbohydrates…

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Biomolecules are the chemical basis of life. Carbohydrates supply and store energy and form structural fibres; proteins (from 20 amino acids) act as enzymes, transporters, contractile and defence molecules in four structural levels; lipids store energy and build membranes; nucleic acids (DNA/RNA) store and express genetic information; enzymes, water and minerals complete the set.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Biomolecules are organic compounds of living organisms — carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids — and the inorganic biomolecules water and essential minerals.  ·  Carbohydrates follow the general formula Cm(H2O)n; monosaccharides (glucose, fructose, galactose) condense into disaccharides (sucrose, lactose, maltose) and polysaccharides (starch, glycogen, cellulose).  ·  Proteins are polymers of 20 amino acids joined by peptide bonds (-CO-NH-), organised into primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary levels of structure.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Lipids are not true polymers; triglycerides, phospholipids, steroids and waxes store energy at about 9 kcal/g, build membranes and act as hormones.  ·  Nucleic acids are polymers of nucleotides (pentose sugar + phosphate + nitrogenous base); DNA stores genetic information while RNA directs protein synthesis.  ·  Enzymes are biological catalysts that lower activation energy without being consumed; most are proteins but some catalytic RNA molecules (ribozymes) also act as enzymes.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: General carbohydrate ratio: C : H : O = 1 : 2 : 1, i.e. (CH2O)n  ·  Endergonic polymerisation (condensation): monomer + monomer → dimer + H2O  ·  Peptide unit: -C(=O)-NH-

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: DNA base pairing: A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3 H-bonds)  ·  Carbohydrate: Cm(H2O)n  ·  Triglyceride: glycerol + 3 fatty acids
